title: MAS bets on 80,000 AI-trained compliance staff — but will it hold up?
summary: MAS commits to upskilling 80,000 financial services workers in AI, and Alex and Jordan disagree sharply on what that means for compliance functions. Plus: Revolut's Argentina acquisition, California's memecoin ban, and a hard deadline for Hong Kong MLROs tonight.
script:
ALEX: Tomorrow is the thirtieth of September, which means tonight is the last night for Hong Kong-regulated authorised institutions to submit their annual AML and CFT self-assessment return to the HKMA. That deadline is not moving. That is where we are starting today. This is AML Agents Briefing for Tuesday the twenty-ninth of September 2026.

JORDAN: Before we go anywhere else, let's be direct about what that self-assessment covers. Under paragraph eleven of the HKMA's AML and CFT Guideline, you are certifying your controls across customer due diligence, ongoing transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, suspicious transaction report filing, training adequacy, governance, and the outputs of your independent audit. That is a wide perimeter. If your independent audit finding was weak and you haven't resolved it, you are about to put that in writing to your supervisor.

ALEX: Right. And the HKMA issued deficiency letters to roughly twenty-five percent of its supervised institution population earlier this year, off the back of the Q4 2025 STR narrative quality thematic review. Those letters are still open. If you are in that cohort and your self-assessment goes in tonight without addressing the STR narrative findings, you are compounding the problem. Your examiner will hold both documents side by side.

JORDAN: So the action for any MLRO at an HKMA-supervised institution who is listening to this on their commute in is simple. Before you submit, check two things. First, confirm your independent audit section reflects any remediation you have actually completed, not remediation you have planned. And second, if you received a deficiency letter on STR narrative quality, make sure there is a cross-reference somewhere in the self-assessment that shows the examiner your remediation trajectory. Silence on a known finding looks worse than a partial fix that is documented.

ALEX: I want to move to the bigger story from yesterday, which is the Monetary Authority of Singapore's AI Workforce Co-Lab announcement. MAS committed on the twenty-eighth to upskilling eighty thousand financial services employees in artificial intelligence. The scale of that number is what I want to sit with. Eighty thousand people. That is not a pilot. That is a structural intervention in how Singapore's financial sector is going to run compliance and risk functions over the next three to five years.

JORDAN: I want to push back on your framing slightly. You're reading this as a structural intervention in compliance. I read it as primarily a capital markets and front-office workforce story that the compliance function is going to have to adapt to, rather than lead. MAS is signalling that it wants AI embedded in financial services broadly. Compliance teams will benefit, but they are not the primary target of this investment.

ALEX: That is a fair challenge. But here is why I think the compliance read matters anyway. If your institution upskills eighty people in AI and none of them sit in the second line, you have just created a capability gap between the business and the people who are supposed to oversee it. MLROs need to be in the room when their institutions are deciding how to allocate those training slots.

JORDAN: That I agree with completely. And practically, the action here is immediate. If you're the head of financial crime compliance at a Singapore-licensed institution, you need to be talking to your chief people officer this week about how compliance roles are being included in the Co-Lab's training allocation. Because if you wait for HR to solve this for you, you will end up with a trading floor full of AI-literate staff and a transaction monitoring team that is still running manual rules from 2022.

ALEX: The second thing worth noting is that MAS pairing this announcement with its existing expectations under Notice 626 and the broader supervisory agenda on technology risk creates an implicit bar. A regulator that is publicly investing this heavily in AI capability across the sector will have progressively less patience for institutions that cite resourcing constraints when their transaction monitoring or sanctions screening is underperforming. The baseline for what counts as adequate is moving.

JORDAN: And I'd add, your quarterly STR governance review under Notice 626 Section 6 should already be on your desk. We flagged that obligation weeks ago. If it isn't done, add it to the list alongside the HKMA submission.

ALEX: Shifting our focus, Revolut has received regulatory approval to acquire Banco Cetelem Argentina from BNP Paribas. This is Revolut's first licensed banking presence in Latin America. I want to be honest: on its face this is an M&A story. But the compliance read is real.

JORDAN: It is. Argentina brings a genuinely complicated risk profile. Capital controls, a dual exchange rate regime for most of its recent history, elevated informal economy activity. Revolut is very good at onboarding customers quickly. That operational model under Argentine conditions, with Revolut's global customer base potentially routing through a licensed Argentine entity, is a combination that will attract supervisory attention from multiple directions.

ALEX: The FATF mutual evaluation calendar for Argentina is worth watching in this context. And for any compliance professional at a correspondent bank that currently has or is considering a relationship with Revolut's Argentine entity, the read-across is straightforward. Your correspondent banking due diligence framework needs to account for the jurisdiction risk layered onto the Revolut business model. Those two things together require a more granular assessment than either would alone.

JORDAN: Quickly on California's memecoin legislation, which Governor Newsom signed yesterday. This is sub-federal, so its direct reach is limited. But it is the first time a United States jurisdiction has categorically excluded an entire digital asset class by product type rather than by the conduct of individual actors. For compliance teams at virtual asset service providers with any United States nexus, the legal analysis of what counts as a memecoin under California's definition now has regulatory consequences. That is new.

ALEX: And the Solana exchange-traded fund inflows story, one hundred and eighty-eight million dollars in a week with Bitwise taking roughly two-thirds, matters primarily because it confirms institutional capital is moving into Solana-based products at scale. For AML teams at crypto asset service providers, that means your know-your-transaction coverage of Solana inflows needs to be at the same standard as your Ethereum and Bitcoin coverage. If it isn't, now is the time to test it.

JORDAN: Before we close, one more thing for Hong Kong listeners specifically. If you get your self-assessment in tonight and you think the hard work is done, it isn't. The HKMA's STR thematic review deficiency letters are still open, and the clock on closure is running. Do not let the submission deadline become a reason to deprioritise the underlying remediation.

ALEX: Tomorrow, watch for any follow-up guidance from MAS on the AI Co-Lab's scope and eligible programmes. That detail will tell you whether compliance roles are explicitly included or whether you need to make the case internally yourself. Full source links and the obligation register for the next ninety days are at amlagents dot streamlit dot app. See you Wednesday.
